rationale: The hypothesis posits a strict genotype-phenotype dichotomy in which biallelic truncating/loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 exclusively lead to severe prenatal akinesia with generalized arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC), whereas missense variants (such as p.Pro1133Leu) preserve partial function and manifest primarily as progressive core-like congenital myopathy without severe contractures. However, detailed examination of the foundational cohorts reveals that Roos et al. (2023) identified five patients across four consanguineous families presenting with congenital myopathy, neurological defects, and dysmorphic features harboring two homozygous missense and two homozygous nonsense (truncating) variants. The occurrence of truncating (nonsense) alleles within the congenital myopathy/neurodevelopmental cohort of Roos et al. directly conflicts with the hypothesis that truncating variants invariably cause severe generalized AMC/prenatal akinesia, indicating that phenotypic expressivity spans a spectrum rather than a clean bifurcation based purely on variant class.

evidence.text: Schnabel et al. identified five affected individuals from three independent consanguineous families harboring homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 who presented with generalized arthrogryposis multiplex congenita affecting the shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee, and foot, accompanied by microcephaly, scoliosis, reduced palmar/plantar skin creases, and dysmorphic facies.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism. Using exome sequencing, we identified homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 in all patients.

numbers.metric: affected individuals with homozygous truncating variants and generalized contractures

evidence.text: Roos et al. identified five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with bi-allelic FILIP1 variants causing a syndromic disorder characterized by congenital myopathy, brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness, and dysmorphism; however, this cohort included two nonsense (truncating) and two missense variants, contradicting the claim that truncating variants strictly produce arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: Here, we report on five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense and two missense)... Patients exhibit a broad spectrum of neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology and dysmorphic features. Electron and immunofluorescence microscopy on the muscle biopsy derived from the patient harbouring the homozygous p.[Pro1133Leu] missense variant revealed core-like zones of myofibrillar disintegration, autophagic vacuoles and accumulation of FLNc.

evidence.text: Chaurasia et al. screened large exome datasets and corroborated that homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 are associated with syndromic arthrogryposis with microcephaly, while also recognizing FILIP1 as a causative gene for congenital myopathy.

source.title: Systematic analysis of homozygous autosomal copy number losses in exomes improves diagnostic yield and uncovers ultra-rare recessive disorders
source.quote: Further analysis of the data and identification of additional affected individuals through collaboration led to identification of biallelic FILIP1 and FAM177A1 variants as causes of a syndromic arthrogryposis and a neuromuscular disorder respectively.

evidence.text: Characterization of FILIP-knockout animal models demonstrates muscle weakness (reduced grip strength) and sensory nociceptive defects alongside cortical development perturbation, confirming systemic neuromusculoskeletal pathology resulting from total loss of FILIP1.

source.title: Deletion of filamin A-interacting protein (FILIP) results in a weak grip strength and abnormal responses to nociceptive stimulation
source.quote: Our results showed that FILIP-knockout mice exhibited weak grip strength and sensory abnormalities. Interestingly, we also found that FILIP was expressed in a subset of neurons in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG).

conflicts: Schnabel et al. (2023) established that homozygous truncating variants cause severe generalized arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (AMC) with microcephaly (5/5 patients across 3 families), whereas Roos et al. (2023) described homozygous nonsense (truncating) variants presenting within a spectrum of congenital myopathy, dysmorphic features, and neurodevelopmental delay rather than primary prenatal akinesia AMC, refuting a clear-cut binary genotype-phenotype split between truncating and missense variants.

new_directions.question_text: Does the specific position of truncating variants along the FILIP1 transcript (e.g., escaping versus triggering nonsense-mediated decay, or sparing specific filamin-A versus filamin-C binding motifs) determine whether the clinical outcome is arthrogryposis multiplex congenita versus congenital core myopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Because nonsense variants appear in both AMC cohorts and congenital myopathy cohorts, variant position and domain architecture disruption must be correlated with expression levels and functional filamin binding.

new_directions.question_text: Do muscle biopsies from patients presenting with FILIP1-associated arthrogryposis multiplex congenita exhibit the same core-like zones of myofibrillar disintegration and FLNc aggregation observed in missense-associated congenital myopathy?
new_directions.rationale: Comparing the histopathological ultrastructure and proteomic aggregation signatures across patients presenting with AMC versus myopathy will determine whether they represent distinct cellular mechanisms or varying degrees of the same primary myopathy.
